steps.title: Heal drifted knowledge notes
steps.instructions:
The knowledge graph has partial drift: some notes describe code that has since changed, most have not. Your job is to heal exactly the drifted ones in place — never a wholesale re-derivation of the graph (that is what docs/kb-build-parallel.plan.json is for, and this run has no such step to fall back on).

STEP 1 — find the candidates. Call memory_search broadly enough to surface the corpus (e.g. by subsystem/category, or a query matching your project's area notes). Every result carries a Currency line naming the ratio, e.g. 'Currency: N of M checkable note(s) describe code that has since changed'; the search result's own `drifted` array names the note ids. Collect every id memory_search flags drifted. If a search leaves `drifted` empty or absent, run another query — do not conclude the graph is clean from one narrow search.

STEP 2 — judge each candidate. For EVERY drifted id: memory_read it in full (not just the summary you already saw), then read the paths it declares against the CURRENT tree — the actual files, not what the note claims about them. Judge whether the note's prose is still an accurate description of what those files do now.

STEP 3 — act, per the same two verbs the auditor role always uses:
  - Prose FALSIFIED by the tree → HEAL: memory_write the SAME id with what the code says now. A correction rewrites the WHOLE retrieval surface — title and summary too, not only the body and claims: the summary is what every later searcher reads first, and a healed body under a stale summary ships the retired claim to everyone who never opens the note. This is a rewrite of the existing note, never a second note.
  - Prose STILL TRUE of the tree → CONFIRM: call memory_verify with its id. One call, no rewrite — declaring it verified is the whole act. Rewriting a note you did not change claims authorship you don't have and buys nothing.
  - If you cannot form a judgment (the declared paths no longer exist, or the note is ambiguous about what it covers), leave it: do not guess, and name it in your summary as left with why.

You make NO other repository changes — this plan writes to the knowledge graph only, never to source files.

STEP 4 — end with a summary that lists three groups by note id: HEALED (memory_write issued, with a one-line reason each), VERIFIED (memory_verify issued), and LEFT (skipped, with why). A drifted id missing from all three groups is a defect in your own run — account for every candidate STEP 1 collected.
